inputBoundaryInventory.summary: The audit target is a Flask/FAB application, so input boundaries are its own HTTP endpoints plus task/CLI/file boundaries: (1) the HTTP surface - 199 @expose REST handlers in 52 per-domain api.py files (marshmallow-schema loads of request.json at e.g. superset/charts/api.py:324 add_model_schema.load(request.json), request.args.get reads at 51 sites, request.form reads at 70 sites incl. import flows with json.loads(request.form['passwords']) at charts/api.py:1098-1115 and json.loads(request.form['form_data']) at charts/data/api.py:225, request.files.get at 7 sites, request.cookies/headers at 3+3 sites), FAB @rison query parsing injected as kwargs['rison'] and read via kwargs['rison'] (32 sites) / kwargs.get('rison') (1 site), route path variables as @expose handler parameters (pk/client_id/digest/dashboard_id_or_slug), and the single @app.route health endpoint (views/health.py); (2) the task boundary - 10 @celery_app.task/@shared_task functions whose parameters carry request-derived payloads; (3) the CLI boundary - click commands (76 decorator sites) in superset/cli; (4) the filesystem - open() (17 sites) and .read() for import/export YAML/ZIP bundle processing; (5) the database itself - stored RLS filter clauses, dataset WHERE/HAVING/sql expressions and jinja-rendered query templates are re-interpolated into SQL (intermediate propagation, not external input); (6) current_app.config (83 reads) and os.environ (13 reads) - operator-level trust. The dominant SQL execution channels are: cursor.execute (DBAPI cursors from Database.get_raw_connection, models/core.py:531, BaseEngineSpec.execute at db_engine_specs/base.py:1551 and 20+ engine-spec overrides like hive.py:548/:631, postgres.py:312/:418/:433, presto.py:347/:810, mysql.py:282/:297, snowflake.py:239/:254, gsheets.py:117, ocient.py:389, trino.py:250, connectors/sqla/utils.py:156), engine.execute (hive.py:210/:232, impala.py:74, models/dashboard.py:367/:384 via db.engine.execute), session/connection.execute of SQLAlchemy Core constructs (security/manager.py 21 sites, common/tags.py 5 sites), pd.read_sql_query (3 execution sites), sqlalchemy text()/TextAsFrom construction (base.py:557/:871/:1405, utils/encrypt.py:175, self.text()/get_text_clause wrappers in models/helpers.py:1077 and connectors/sqla/models.py:1095 feeding template-processed WHERE/HAVING/RLS clauses at helpers.py:806/:816/:1918/:1936 and sqla/models.py:1069/:1079). Roughly 90 execute-family call sites exist under superset/ outside migrations; ORM filter()/order_by() paths compile to parameterized SQL and are not modeled as raw sinks, while db_engine_specs frequently f-string-interpolate identifiers and cancel IDs directly into executed SQL.

extraction.executionPlan: codeql query run (sequential, one at a time) + codeql bqrs decode --format=csv; NOT database analyze / SARIF. Execution is deferred to the next round per the task contract (generation only).
extraction.metadataForm: plain multi-column select queries carrying @name/@description/@id/@tags only; intentionally no @kind problem (wrong shape for multi-column candidate tables) and no @kind table (not assumed to exist).
columnContract: node (location-backed AST node; decodes as file:line:col)
arg_index (0-based positional argument index, -1 when not applicable)
match_kind ('api' = resolved real API call via API graphs, 'ast' = syntax-level match)

matchKindSemantics.api: call resolved through semmle.python.ApiGraphs; in this project NO sink or source row is expected to resolve at API level: SQL execution flows through local cursor/engine/connection variables and wrapper chains (conn.cursor(), engine.raw_connection(), db_engine_spec.execute(...), self.text(...)) that API graphs cannot bind to driver members, and the flask request object / click options / celery payloads are framework-injected values, not module members. The column is kept for cross-project contract consistency.
matchKindSemantics.ast: pure AST shape match (attribute/name text, syntactic receiver, request/kwargs/config/environ name conventions). All .execute(...) matching is receiver-name-agnostic (any <obj>.execute(...) matches), which tolerates cursor/engine/session aliasing but cannot prove the receiver executes SQL - name-collision noise (e.g. future.execute, plan.execute) is possible and is left to the labeling step.

extraction.expectedVolume: roughly 1500-2600 source rows (request state attribute/get/subscript/whole-mapping reads ~200, kwargs['rison'] ~33, @expose handler parameters ~900-1100 across 199 handlers, @app.route handler parameters ~1, click command parameters ~150-250 across ~60 commands plus ~50 option registrations, celery task parameters ~30, env ~13, config ~85, file open/read ~60-120, internal_transfer call arguments ~200-700) and roughly 250-450 sink rows (90 execute-family call sites + 3 pd.read_sql_query sites + bound_params companion rows + text-clause construction sites ~24 + f-string/concat/format construction nodes ~40-120 + internal SQL wrapper functions ~60-120 + ~12 sql_api_def definition rows). This is in line with prior projects in this series (django ~3500-5500/~500-900, pgadmin4 2150/61, arches ~1500-2500/~200-400, maltrail 617/52).

uncoveredCases: Positional-argument scan cap: the internal_transfer family enumerates argument positions 0-9 (i is bound by range membership before the indexed Call.getPositionalArg(i) lookup, because the index parameter of getPositionalArg is a checked/total-function input in QL); calls with more than 10 positional arguments would not be scanned. No such call was observed on the SQL-relevant paths in this snapshot.

BaseEngineSpec.execute call-site argument positions: the engine-spec adapter is a classmethod execute(cls, cursor, query, **kwargs) - at call sites like db_engine_spec.execute(cursor, statement) (sql_lab.py) and cls.execute(cursor, sql, async_=True) (base.py:1069) the SQL text is positional argument 1, NOT argument 0. The generic receiver-agnostic sink row reports arg_index 0 (correct for DBAPI cursor.execute / engine.execute / session.execute, where SQL is argument 0); the bound_params companion row reports arg_index 1; and the sql_api_def definition row for BaseEngineSpec.execute records the true SQL-text parameter position 2 (after cls and cursor). The labeling step must reconcile these.

pd.read_sql_query keyword form: 2 of the 3 execution sites pass SQL as the sql= keyword (models/helpers.py:1365, connectors/sqla/models.py:817), so the row's arg_index 0 refers to the sql parameter semantically, not to an actual positional argument; the positional form appears at connectors/sqla/models.py:170.

Handler detection is decorator-name-based: functions decorated with @expose (any import alias) or @app.route are treated as handlers; a handler whose request is accessed through a different proxy alias (e.g. `from flask import request as req`) would be missed - no such alias was observed. Parameters of @protect/@safe/@rison decorators themselves are not sources (the @rison-injected value is captured separately via the kwargs['rison']/kwargs.get('rison') reads).

FAB @rison injection is framework-internal (flask_appbuilder is not part of this database); the boundary visible in this tree is the kwargs['rison'] read. Endpoints decorated with @rison that never read kwargs['rison'] (value consumed only via the schema-validated decorator argument) are not captured - all 35 @rison sites were checked against 33 kwargs['rison'] reads.

Keyword-argument hand-offs into SQL wrapper functions (e.g. execute_sql_statements(rendered_query=...) or **kwargs propagation into BaseEngineSpec.execute(query=...)) are not captured by internal_transfer (positional arguments only); the DBAPI kwargs path (cursor.execute(query, **kwargs) at hive.py:548) is likewise not decomposed.

Jinja template rendering (superset/jinja_context.py, superset/common/*.py process_template) is the dominant SQL-text construction mechanism for SQL Lab / chart queries (rendered_query, WHERE/HAVING/RLS clauses, sql metrics) but produces the SQL text through template evaluation, not string operators: it is NOT captured by the construction family; the rendered values enter the extraction as internal_transfer arguments into execute_sql_statements/render and as self.text(...) text-clause rows at the consumption sites. Sandboxed Jinja is a sanitizer candidate for the labeling step, not an extraction rule here.

Variable-template %-formatting / .format() on SQL variables where the template is a variable (not a literal) is not captured by the construction family (literal-template shapes only); such sites are still represented by their execute/text-clause rows.

Cross-function construction (SQL built in one function, executed in another) is not traced at extraction time; the construction family only covers constructions directly executed as argument 0 of an execute-family/read_sql_query/text-clause call, or located inside a function that directly executes SQL or builds a TextClause.

Dynamic receiver identity: <obj>.execute(...) / .text(...) matching is syntactic; whether the receiver is a DBAPI cursor, a SQLAlchemy engine/connection/session, an engine-spec class, or an unrelated object with an execute/text method is not resolved (e.g. future.execute() style collisions are possible). Receiver hints (cursor/conn/engine/session/db/self/db_engine_spec) are emitted for the labeling step.

sqlparse.format(sql, ...) calls inside SQL wrapper functions would match the .format() construction shape by member name (sqlparse is a SQL pretty-printer, not a constructor); at most a handful of such rows (base.py:894/:1417, postgres.py:271, connectors/sqla/models.py:845/:916) and they carry the SQL text being reformatted - retained as low-risk noise for the labeling step.
